about: Vectors for the port claim and the port choice (DEC-0154 HA-1, DEC-0160), written by tools/vectors/port-claim.ts, never by hand. fileName: claimFileName(service, account), .passioncode-ports.<service>.<account>.json. read: readClaims(files, presentAccounts), each file {name, owner, json} as a reader finds it in the shared folder (owner the file owner's uid, its SID on Windows); the answer is {claims, notes}: the usable claims in the order read, and one note {code, file} per ignored file, the first that applies in this order: claim-invalid (not a passioncode-port-claim/1 document, updatedAt a real UTC instant), claim-name-mismatch (the name is not claimFileName of the content's service and account), claim-owner-mismatch (the owner is not the account it names), claim-account-absent (the account is not in presentAccounts). choose: choosePort(input) with input.claims = readClaims(input.files, input.presentAccounts).claims; descriptors are this account's services directory, any service, as {service, instance, port}; listeners every listener accepting on 127.0.0.1:<port>, a wildcard bind (0.0.0.0, [::]) included, as {port, account}: the caller lists a wildcard bind among them, and no vector carries an address; ownListener whether this instance's own listener holds the recorded port; squatted whether this account's own claim path exists with another owner, and then no claim is read. The answer is {port, kept, reason, notes} or {fault: no-free-port, notes}; reason kept-own-listener, kept-free, new-none-recorded, or new-held-by- followed by the first holder of the recorded port in the order descriptor, claim-other-account, claim-other-service, listener; a new port is the first candidate no listener, no other id.instance's descriptor, and no claim of another account or of another service in this account names; notes holds claim-path-squatted when squatted. rebuild: rebuildClaim({account, service, descriptors, ownState, now}): the ports of this service's descriptors in the account and its own state, once each, ascending, in a claim with updatedAt now; {delete: true} when none remains; {fault: claim-invalid} when that claim would not be a valid passioncode-port-claim/1 document (more than 64 ports, a port outside 1 to 65535, an account that is not a uid or a SID, now not a UTC instant with Z); the old claim is never read. A service is at most 130 characters and an account at most 100, so a file name is at most 255 bytes.

fileName.name: a service id and a uid
an app's part and a uid
a service id and a SID
two parts of one app in one account: two files
two parts of one app in one account: the other part's file
the longest service and account: 255 bytes

read.name: a claim of this account and one of another: both kept, in the order read
an app's part with two ports
a Windows claim, its owner the SID it names
a claim whose owner is not its account: ignored
a uid with a leading zero: invalid, never compared with the owner's uid
a claim of an account no longer on the computer: ignored
a name that names another account than the content: ignored
a name that names another service than the content: ignored
a member beyond the five: invalid
no port: invalid (a claim with no port is deleted)
port 0: invalid
port 65536: invalid
a port that is not an integer: invalid
a port named twice: invalid
65 ports: invalid
an account named by its login name: invalid
a service id with an upper-case letter and no dot: invalid
updatedAt with an offset: invalid
updatedAt on a day that does not exist: invalid
another schema revision: invalid
content that is not an object: invalid
invalid content and another owner: invalid is named first
a wrong name and another owner: the name is named first
another owner and an absent account: the owner is named first
the longest service and account: kept
a service of 131 characters: invalid (the file name would pass 255 bytes)
an account of 101 characters: invalid (the file name would pass 255 bytes)
one ignored claim among usable ones

choose.name: no port recorded: the first free candidate
the recorded port free: kept
held by its own listener: kept
its own descriptor declares it: kept
held by another id.instance's descriptor: a new port
held by another instance of this service: a new port
its own listener holds it and another id.instance's descriptor declares it: a new port
named by another account's claim: a new port
named by another account's claim while its own listener holds it: kept
held by another account's listener: a new port
held by a listener of this account that is not this instance's: a new port
listeners of another account on the recorded port and the next candidate: the candidate after them
a claim of an absent account: ignored, the port kept
a claim whose owner is not its account: ignored, the port kept
a claim path held by another owner: claims are not read, the port kept, the path reported
a claim path held by another owner, no port recorded: a candidate another account claims is taken
a claim path held by another owner: the listener test still holds
a claim path held by another owner: the descriptor test still holds
a claim aged out (its file missing): the port kept while free
this service's own claim names the recorded port: kept
this account's claim of another service (an app with no descriptor origin) names the recorded port: a new port while that app is not listening
this account's claim of another service names a candidate: the next candidate
this account's claim of another service while its own listener holds it: kept
two instances of one service, one restarts: its port kept, the other's port not taken
two instances of one service, the second without a port: it skips the first's
two parts of one app in one account (one per data folder): a part skips the port the other part claims
two parts of one app in one account: a part keeps its own port beside the other's claim
a candidate named only by this service's own claim: taken
holder order: a descriptor is named before a claim and a listener
holder order: another account's claim before this account's claim of another service and a listener
holder order: this account's claim of another service before a listener
a held recorded port and every candidate held: no free port
no port recorded and no candidate free: no free port
no candidates at all: no free port
a squatted path and no free candidate: the fault carries the note
on Windows, another account's claim by SID: a new port

rebuild.name: two instances of which one restarts: both ports
another service's descriptors in the account are not this claim's
a claim aged out: the rebuild writes the port back
an app without a descriptor origin: the port in its own state
an app's part with two ports out of order and one twice: sorted, once each
a descriptor's port also in its own state: once
uninstall of one of two instances: the remaining one's port, the removed one's state never read
uninstall of the last instance: the claim is deleted
only another service's descriptor remains: the claim is deleted
on Windows, the account by SID
one of two parts of one app in one account: only its own state, never the other part's claim
one of two parts of one app loses its last port: only its claim is deleted
65 ports: a fault, no claim written
port 0 in its own state: a fault, no claim written
an account named by its login name: a fault, no claim written
now with an offset: a fault, no claim written
